absent: Locking or ordering rules guarding global mitigation states, policy globals, and system bitmap against concurrent enablement and sysfs reads.
Full layout and valid values of control table, hardening data, capability descriptor, and alternative patch descriptor structures beyond fields observed.
Behavior of timestamp counter setter, SSBS detection, and dynamic versus forced mitigation predicates not shown in fragments.
Exact sysfs output spellings and prctl numeric encodings beyond paraphrased meanings.
Assignment and lifetime of per-CPU vector cache and hypervisor slot values across boot, hotplug, and guest transitions.
Derivation of CSV2P3 and clear-BHB support predicates and sanitised register infrastructure.

findings.text: Early init hook attempts to register an ABI sysctl table and reports invalid argument when registration yields no table.
Parent abi hosts one integer control named tagged_addr_disabled with read write permission and inclusive bounds zero to one handled as an integer vector with min max policy.

Loader protection adjustment leaves the input unchanged unless interpreter presence matches expectation and ELF flags carry BTI; when both hold, executable mappings gain BTI while others stay unchanged.

Timestamp counter mode query and update reject compatibility tasks; the query reflects a per-thread flag as either SEGV or enabled value delivered to user memory, while the update delegates to a separate setter after the same compatibility check.
Variant one sysfs show always presents a fixed mitigated presentation attributing protection to user pointer cleansing.
Global variant two state is paired with a mostly-read disable flag set by an early boot parameter parser.

Variant two sysfs show combines global variant two state with BHB state and unprivileged eBPF availability to select among not affected, vulnerable, and mitigated presentations with predictor hardening wording plus an optional BHB suffix.
Accessor returns the current global BHB mitigation state without side effects.
Hardware safety for variant two is decided first by CSV2 feature presence and otherwise by membership in a fixed allowlist of unaffected cores; absence from both means vulnerable.
Firmware probe for workaround one maps firmware success to mitigated, firmware unaffected to unaffected, and unsupported or unknown replies to vulnerable.
Variant two capability probe expects local CPU scope in non-preemptible context and reports presence unless hardware or firmware probes deem the CPU unaffected.
Accessor returns the current global variant two mitigation state.
Per-CPU hardening record holds a callback pointer and a hypervisor vector slot; the installer updates both on the local CPU but omits vector work when hypervisor mode is unavailable.
Two small non-instrumented helpers trigger architecture workaround one through SMC and HVC conduits respectively with no result handling.

Software selector returns a link-stack cleansing routine only on two Falkor model identifiers and null elsewhere; the routine preserves the return address while issuing a short repeated call sequence.

Variant two enablement checks hardware first then firmware, honors a global off switch, chooses a conduit-specific callback with CPU-specific override, installs it, and folds the outcome into global state.
Variant three-a presence is true only for A57 and A72 class cores; enablement advances the local hardening slot toward indirect vectors when the corresponding capability is present.
Variant four policy distinguishes dynamic, forced enabled, and forced disabled modes stored in a mostly-read global, plus a per-CPU flag indicating SSBD callback need and a global mitigation state.
Boot option accepts three textual selectors for force on, force off, and kernel dynamic handling; empty or unmatched input is rejected as invalid.
Store bypass sysfs show maps unaffected, mitigated, and vulnerable or unknown global states to three distinct presentations.
Accessor returns the current global variant four mitigation state.
Variant four capability probe expects local scope without preemption and reports presence unless hardware says unaffected and firmware concurs when consulted.

Early alternative patch for firmware mitigation enablement acts on a single instruction slot and converts branch to no-operation only for dynamic policy when SSBS is absent and mitigations are not disabled.
Conduit patch rewrites a single no-operation slot to the hypercall or secure-call encoding matching the detected conduit and leaves it unchanged when conduit is unknown.

Architecture prctl query supports only the store bypass selector and otherwise reports no device; its helper maps global state and per-task SSBD flags to not-affected, enable, or prctl-qualified disable variants.
BHB defenses are encoded as four bit positions for loop, firmware, hardware, and instruction mechanisms tracked in a system-wide bitmap alongside a global BHB state.
BHB safety uses a fixed allowlist of unaffected cores with a sticky global flag that answers non-local queries once any CPU proved unsafe.
Loop hardening strengths are fixed small integers per microarchitecture grouping with values 8, 11, 24, 32, 38 and 132, defaulting to zero when no group matches.
BHB firmware availability requires both a non-none conduit and a firmware query for workaround three returning success; other replies map to unaffected or vulnerable.

ECBHB support is read from a local or sanitised feature register depending on scope; the BHB affected verdict exempts CSV2P3 and allowlisted cores and otherwise records the maximum loop count unless clear-BHB is available.

BHB enablement is skipped when unaffected or when variant two remains vulnerable or when configuration or command line disables it; otherwise it selects the first available among hardware, instruction, loop, and firmware paths, updating vectors, slots, and bitmap, and clears superseded firmware callbacks when the firmware path supersedes workaround one.
Per-CPU vector installer caches the chosen hardening vector locally and programs the vector base with barrier except when kernel page-table isolation defers switching to the exit path.
Two non-instrumented patch helpers each expect a single instruction slot and emit a no-operation only when the corresponding loop or firmware bitmap bit is set.

Loop count patch decodes the destination register from the original move and re-encodes a sixty-four-bit zeroing move-wide carrying the global maximum count, doing nothing when branch-history defense is not configured.

Move-wide encoder builds zero, keep, or inverse variants for thirty-two or sixty-four-bit forms, validating immediate range, shift alignment, and variant, and returns a fault encoding with diagnostic on misuse.
Capability and affected probes require local CPU scope without preemption and patch helpers require single-instruction slots; violation triggers warnings or fatal checks.
